solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Weapon control precedes conflict

indicators.note: one thing preceding another tells the solver to set the first piece before the second

parts.note: to have a hand in something is to have control of it
a jar is a clash or discord, as in jarring opinions

explanation.surface: A general reflection that military control comes before fighting breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: A handjar is a broad-bladed Persian dagger or short sword, so it is a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Slight coughs one gets in early winter

definitions.note: 'early' marks an old word: Shakespeare's Latin name for the season

indicators.note: something that gets in enters another thing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a hem is a small throat-clearing cough
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone notices the first small coughs of the cold season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early' is not a selection signal here; it marks the answer as an archaic word, the Latin for the season used by Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiems is the Latin name for the cold season, used in older English poetry such as Love's Labour's Lost.

clue.text: Classical giant pilasters Susa only half erected

parts.note: antae are square pilasters at the ends of a temple wall

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting something upright means reading it from the bottom up
taking only half of a word keeps just its first two letters of four

parts.note: the first half of the ancient Persian city's name

explanation.surface: Archaeologists only half rebuild columns at the ancient city of Susa, a giant task.
explanation.definitionFit: Antaeus was the giant of Greek myth, son of Poseidon and Gaia, whom Hercules wrestled and lifted off the earth.

clue.text: One of the awkward ones mostly high up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters run from bottom to top
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: high is slang for intoxicated

explanation.surface: Socially awkward people are said to be mostly found high up, perhaps in ivory towers.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurd is a variant spelling of nerd, a socially inept or awkward person.

clue.text: Help with Labour party unionist answer about left

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
U is the standard abbreviation for unionist

indicators.note: turning about sends the pair of letters the other way round

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A political note about a Labour party event helped by a unionist.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes Labour look like the British political party; it is childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: A doula is a trained companion who supports a woman through childbirth, giving non-medical help during labour.

clue.text: Legal expert gentleman elevated over magistrate in project

indicators.note: the combined pieces sit inside the outer word

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed over another simply comes first
in a down entry, raising a word means reading its letters upwards

parts.note: sir is the title for a gentleman
a consul was a chief magistrate of the Roman republic

explanation.surface: A legal expert, a gentleman promoted above a magistrate, takes part in a project.
explanation.walkthrough: Project looks like a noun, a scheme; it is the verb to stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: A jurisconsult is a person learned in law, especially civil or international law, whose opinions are sought.

clue.text: Empty rage against particular type of antibody

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word rage
agin is a dialect form of against

explanation.surface: Pointless anger directed at a particular antibody, as an allergy sufferer might feel.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagin is an antibody of the type involved in allergic reactions, chiefly the IgE class.

clue.text: Rarely get comfortable before college function

indicators.note: one piece placed before another sets them side by side in that order

parts.note: cose is a rare verb meaning to make oneself cosy
C is an abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A student seldom settles in comfortably before going up to college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' is not a frequency but a dictionary label: the verb is a rare one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosec is the short name for the cosecant, a trigonometric function, the reciprocal of the sine.

clue.text: Doctor discerns free hysterics

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are falsified into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician recognises an outbreak of uncontrolled hysteria.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor reads as a medical person in a scene about hysterics, but it is the verb meaning to tamper.
explanation.definitionFit: Crise de nerfs is French for an attack of nerves, an emotional outburst or fit of hysteria.

clue.text: Ring in right hours following old church service

indicators.note: the circle goes inside the abbreviation for hours
the built-up piece comes after the old one in reading order

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for old
RT is an abbreviation for right
HRS is the usual abbreviation for hours
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A bell is rung at the right hours after an old church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Orthros is a Greek word for daybreak; the service is sung before dawn, which the solver may not know from Western usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthros is the morning office of the Eastern Orthodox Church, comparable to Western matins.

clue.text: Monkey takes in afternoon in our nut tree

indicators.note: taking something in means swallowing it, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: the sai is a South American capuchin monkey

indicators.note: the short abbreviation goes inside the possessive word

parts.note: taken as written
A is a dictionary abbreviation for afternoon

explanation.surface: A monkey spends the afternoon in the nut tree in our garden.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside OUR, and that whole piece goes inside the monkey's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The saouari, or souari, is a tall South American tree yielding large edible souari nuts.

clue.text: Austrian instrument with missing lead in Swiss lab

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the name of the laboratory

parts.note: CERN is the particle physics laboratory near Geneva

indicators.note: a word missing its lead has lost its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before losing its front

explanation.surface: An Austrian musical instrument, lacking a leading player, turns up in a Swiss laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a link word but is the fodder: it loses its W and the rest goes inside CERN after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cithern, or cittern, is a wire-strung instrument of the cither family, the zither of Austrian folk music being its relative.

clue.text: Farrier working for top end racer?

indicators.note: something working is in operation and moving, so the letters are set in motion into a new order

parts.note: a smith who shoes horses, taken as written

explanation.surface: A blacksmith toils to shoe a top-class racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: A farrier suggests a racehorse; the racer is a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferrari is the Italian maker of high-performance sports and Formula One cars, a racing machine of the highest class.

clue.text: Land north of Rome and once there one's in a lot of country

parts.note: et is Latin for and, the tongue spoken there once

indicators.note: one's in means the single letter is placed inside the next piece

parts.note: most of the word rural, as in country life
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A description of an ancient region north of Rome and of what lay within that countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: RURA is rural with its last letter cut, signalled by 'a lot of'; I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Etruria was the ancient territory of the Etruscans, in what is now Tuscany, lying to the north of Rome.

clue.text: Writ wrong in law with Latin for Regina

indicators.note: one letter for another means swapping it into that letter's place

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
L is an abbreviation for Latin
R stands for Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A legal note on a wrongful writ, with the Latin used in place of the queen's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tolt was an old English writ by which a case was removed from a court baron to a county court.

clue.text: I must be beginning to despair in sending old fruitcake

indicators.note: saying one letter must be another means it is swapped out for that letter

parts.note: mailing is sending by post
the letter taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the first letter of despair

explanation.surface: Someone despairing over posting an elderly fruitcake.
explanation.walkthrough: Fruitcake is slang for a crazy person, not a cake; the first I of MAILING becomes D.
explanation.definitionFit: A madling is an archaic word for a mad person, which is what the slang fruitcake means.

clue.text: Quiet synagogues, Nazareth's last with fifty gone

indicators.note: with something gone, that letter is taken out

parts.note: shul is a Yiddish word for a synagogue

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of Nazareth
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Synagogues in Nazareth fall silent, fifty people having left.
explanation.definitionFit: To shush is to call for quiet or silence someone, so the verb matches quiet used as a command or verb.

clue.text: Request that is accepted by sharp-toothed war ministry?

indicators.note: a thing accepted by another is taken inside it

parts.note: serrate means notched like the teeth of a saw
to ask is to request
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A request is received by a fierce, sharp-toothed government department of war.
explanation.definitionFit: The seraskierate was the office of the seraskier, the Turkish commander-in-chief and minister of war, so a war ministry.

clue.text: What's light from Etna? Purplish-pink — in its interior, note

indicators.note: having something in its interior means holding it inside

parts.note: puce is a brownish purple colour
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A volcano's light-coloured stone, glowing pinkish purple inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Light means low in weight, not brightness: the rock is so porous it can float.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a very light, porous volcanic rock formed from frothy lava, such as that thrown out by Etna.

clue.text: Army regulation about cutting weight which covers gear in transit

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the thing that does this

indicators.note: a piece cutting into a word is inserted in the middle of it

parts.note: pith is weight or importance, as in pith and moment
A is an abbreviation for army
R is an abbreviation for regulation
A is a dictionary abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: A military rule about reducing the weight of kit carried by soldiers on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: Weight is not a measure here but significance, as in Hamlet's enterprises of great pith and moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitarah is an Anglo-Indian box or basket used for carrying clothes on a journey, so it covers gear in transit.

clue.text: Genus of molluscs containing round vibrating membrane

indicators.note: a word containing another holds it inside

parts.note: Mya is the genus of soft-shelled clams
a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: A biologist describes a mollusc group with a round membrane that vibrates.
explanation.definitionFit: The myringa is the eardrum, the tympanic membrane that vibrates when sound waves strike it.

clue.text: One very good English plant coming up, one with hollow leaves

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
so can mean very, as in so good
E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the word runs from bottom to top

parts.note: to set seedlings is to plant them

explanation.surface: A gardener praises a good English plant coming up in the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant looks like a noun in a gardening scene; it is the verb, to set.
explanation.definitionFit: Isoetes is the quillwort genus, aquatic plants whose quill-like leaves contain hollow air channels.

clue.text: Parliament arrest paltry government

parts.note: lag is slang for to arrest or catch
tin can mean cheap and paltry, as in tinpot
G is an abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A parliament arrests a feeble government.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lagting was a division of the Norwegian legislature, and is the parliament of the Faroe Islands.

clue.text: Appearing unshaven is irrational in high-definition

indicators.note: the words go inside the abbreviation for high definition

parts.note: HD is the usual abbreviation for high definition
taken as written
pi is the best-known irrational number

explanation.surface: A stubbly face looks unreasonably bad on a high-definition screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Irrational reads as unreasonable, but it is the irrational number.
explanation.definitionFit: Hispid means covered with stiff bristly hairs, as a stubbly unshaven chin appears.

clue.text: In a plane sitting centrally is backed in design

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the word for design

parts.note: to design is to intend or mean

indicators.note: a word backed is read in the backward direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A passenger is seated in the middle of an aircraft as designed.
explanation.walkthrough: Plane suggests an aircraft; it is a geometric plane through the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesian means lying in the median plane, the one dividing the body down its middle into two halves.

clue.text: Rising nation in a mess as presented in G&S?

definitions.note: the sign, as printed in G&S, is the ampersand

indicators.note: things in a mess are jumbled, so these letters must be put in a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A rising nation in chaos, as a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta might stage it.
explanation.walkthrough: G&S is Gilbert and Sullivan; the definition is the ampersand character joining the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tironian sign is the shorthand symbol for et, ancestor of the ampersand standing between G and S.

clue.text: Mammal's covering it with bristles

indicators.note: a word covering another wraps around it

parts.note: the seal is a marine mammal; the 's means it is doing the covering
't is the old clipped form of it, as in 'tis

explanation.surface: A mammal's coat is covered with bristles.
explanation.definitionFit: Setal means relating to setae, the bristles of an animal or plant.

clue.text: Not new, unknown word of unknown meaning

parts.note: non is the Latin prefix meaning not
N is an abbreviation for new
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An old, obscure word whose meaning nobody knows.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonny is a meaningless refrain word in old songs, as in hey nonny no, so its sense is unknown.

clue.text: Group of fir trees, little ones, not British

indicators.note: not means leave out the letter that follows

parts.note: babies are little ones
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A clump of fir trees, with little ones, that is not native to Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Abies is the botanical genus of the true firs, so it names the group those trees belong to.

clue.text: With very low bow walk near when earl enters

indicators.note: a letter that enters a word goes inside it

parts.note: to step to is to walk up close
E is an abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: Someone bows very low as they approach and an earl comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow suggests a courtly bend; it is the front of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep-to describes a shore or vessel's approach plunging sharply into deep water, so a low bow nears it closely.

clue.text: What's apparently raised outside of Cuzco?

definitions.text: What's apparently raised outside of Cuzco?

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters means reading them upwards

parts.note: app. is a dictionary abbreviation for apparently

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the Peruvian city's name

explanation.surface: A question about livestock bred around the Andean city of Cuzco.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: alpacas are reared in the Andes around Cuzco, and raised means bred.
explanation.definitionFit: The paco is the alpaca, a domesticated South American camelid raised in the Peruvian highlands.

clue.text: Small pig that was quickly skinned

indicators.note: skinning removes the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: pronto means quickly

explanation.surface: A little pig that was hurriedly skinned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That was' marks an obsolete word, so the definition is the old form of runt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ront is an obsolete spelling of runt, the smallest and weakest pig of a litter.

clue.text: Be appropriate, like a wagtail by falling water but not river

parts.note: pert means lively and jaunty, like the bobbing bird

indicators.note: but not means excepting, so the named letter is left out

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher describes a wagtail perched beside a waterfall, though not by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain is to belong or be relevant, and so to be fitting or appropriate.

clue.text: In English, priest caught what Thomas Aquinas is called

indicators.note: something caught is held inside, so the letter is taken into the word

parts.note: Anglic means English
the first letter of Eli, the priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A note that in English a priest was given Aquinas's title.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Aquinas is the Doctor Angelicus of Catholic tradition. The parse is less certain than most: the priest may instead be Eli, with C for caught, set inside the English word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquinas is known as the Angelic Doctor, Doctor Angelicus, for the purity of his thought.

clue.text: Regional hack passionate about all sections

indicators.note: a word placed about others goes round them

parts.note: hot means passionate

indicators.note: the opening sections of the words give their first letters

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A provincial journalist feels strongly about every part of the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Hack suggests a journalist; it is a dry cough.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoast is a dialect word, chiefly Scots and northern English, for a cough, which is what a hack is.

clue.text: Reproach Benin, secretive about return of work

parts.note: DY is Benin's international vehicle registration code, from its old name Dahomey

indicators.note: one word about another wraps round it

parts.note: sly means secretive and furtive

indicators.note: the return of a word sends it back the other way

parts.note: a machine that works is said to go

explanation.surface: Criticism of a West African country secretive about its labour returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyslogy is a rare word for dispraise or censure, the opposite of eulogy, so it means reproach.
